title: Bottom-up Synthesis of Metastable 2D Hexagonal Copper(I) Iodide on Monolayer and within Bilayer Graphene
authors: David Kaiser, Guobin Jia, Janis Köster, Sadegh Ghaderzadeh, Christian E. Halbig, Siegfried Eigler, Andrey Turchanin, Benjamin Dietzek-Ivanšić, Arkady V. Krasheninnikov, Jonathan Plentz, Elena Besley, Ute Kaiser
abstract: Copper(I) iodide (CuI) is a wide-bandgap semiconductor crystallizing in the 3D $γ$-phase under ambient conditions; its layered van der Waals bulk phase $β$-CuI is stable only between 643 and 673 K. The two-dimensional (2D) h-CuI form has been obtained via liquid-phase exfoliation of mechanochemically prepared precursors and via encapsulation between graphene sheets, whereas bottom-up growth of 2D h-CuI on open surfaces has not yet been demonstrated. Here, we report a vapor-phase synthesis of h-CuI directly on low-defect, large-area monolayer and within bilayer reduced oxo-graphene (r-oxo-G) at low temperatures. Using a copper TEM grid as the solid-state precursor for copper, HI-vapor exposure at 40 $°$C initiates nucleation, while annealing at 180 $°$C promotes the growth of extended h-CuI domains. Aberration-corrected HRTEM resolves the atomic structure, local twist angles, and lattice anisotropy of the CuI/r-oxo-G nanohybrid, while STEM-EDX yields a Cu:I ratio consistent with 1:1. First-principles calculations show that van der Waals adhesion to graphene stabilizes the supported hexagonal layer. Under the presented low-temperature precursor conditions, pathways for nucleation of the $γ$-phase are not available, allowing the hexagonal phase to form selectively at the graphene interface. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the heterostructure retains its hexagonal lattice order at 600 K, including on an open monolayer graphene support. The lateral extent of the growth is limited mainly by remaining interfacial adsorbates. These results establish a route to metastable 2D h-CuI on a chemically inert graphene template, which may be useful for wide-bandgap electronic and optoelectronic devices.
summary: This paper reports a novel, low-temperature vapor-phase method to grow metastable 2D hexagonal Copper(I) Iodide (h-CuI) directly onto graphene. The research combines synthesis, advanced microscopy, and DFT/AIMD calculations to confirm the structural integrity and electronic stabilization of this semiconductor/graphene hybrid. This establishes a promising platform for next-generation wide-bandgap electronic and optoelectronic devices.
main_problem: The primary goal was to establish a bottom-up, low-temperature synthesis route for the metastable 2D hexagonal Copper(I) Iodide (h-CuI) directly onto chemically inert graphene templates.
main_result: The authors successfully synthesized and characterized epitaxial h-CuI domains on both monolayer and bilayer reduced oxo-graphene (r-oxo-G) using a vapor-phase process, confirming its stability and structure.
method: The work combines experimental synthesis (HI vapor exposure and annealing) with advanced characterization (HRTEM, STEM-EDX) and theoretical modeling (DFT calculations and AIMD simulations).
model_or_system: The system involves the epitaxial growth of h-CuI, a wide-bandgap semiconductor, on graphene substrates (SLG and BLG). Theoretical studies model the van der Waals adhesion energy and vibrational dynamics within these heterostructures.
key_observables: Atomic structure, local twist angles, lattice anisotropy, Cu:I stoichiometry, van der Waals adhesion energy ($	ext{E}_{	ext{vdW}}$), and Mean-Square Displacements ($	ext{MSD}_{xy}, 	ext{MSD}_z$).
important_parameters: Low synthesis temperatures ($180^\circ	ext{C}$), which prevent the formation of the bulk $\gamma$-phase; the stabilization energy provided by van der Waals adhesion.
main_assumptions: The growth is limited by remaining interfacial adsorbates, and AIMD simulations are restricted to specific time segments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the two-step synthesis process, structural characterization of the graphene templates, and the resulting epitaxial growth of h-CuI on the graphene layers.
paper_structure: The paper details the synthesis method, presents structural characterization comparing growth on SLG vs. BLG, quantifies the adhesion energy using DFT, and analyzes the thermal stability and vibrational properties using AIMD simulations.
why_interesting: The study provides a detailed understanding of interfacial electronic and structural coupling between a semiconductor and a 2D material, which is crucial for designing novel heterostructures for optoelectronics.

figures.caption: Figure 1. h-CuI synthesis on graphene supported by a copper TEM grid. In the first step, HI treatment at 40 °C forms, through van der Waals stabilization, monolayer h-CuI on graphene; during this step the oxo-graphene template (oxo-G) is reduced to r-oxo-G simultaneously. Annealing at 180 °C then promotes the epitaxial growth of extended h-CuI crystals on graphene. The atom types are indicated at the bottom.
